body:
**Consolidated status 2026-09-07 (2 sessions)** — branch `target-verification-and-lilipod-v2`, head `a8545ee`. *(This comment replaces all earlier text on this thread.)*

## Session 1: target settlements + lilipod v2
The paper §12 ask, answered on the real runtime: `uid_map 0→1000`, `setgroups deny`, shared with init; bare census confirming every §3.3 N+F row (clone flags permitted; mount/pivot_root/unshare/setns/ptrace/umount2 EPERM; unmapped-id chown EINVAL; whiteout-mknod quirk); a **third mechanism M** (path-scoped write allowlist — `/` vs `/tmp` falsifies mapping as the discriminator); `clone(CLONE_NEWUTS)`+sethostname works → per-container hostnames. Harness bug found+fixed: `probe check` now exits non-zero.

lilipod v2.3 (`patches/lilipod-restricted-v2.diff`, +532/−34): exec root-caused+fixed; §10.2 probe protocol implemented; `Credential{NoSetGroups:true}`; empty-netns trap avoided; `/dev/null` shim; docker-semantics resolv.conf; per-layer `ApplyOCIWhiteouts`. Ten-distro PoC sweep (alpine→fedora), fixup matrix in `poc-note.md`.

## Session 2: extended corpus (paper §3.7a + §11a, evidence `verification/real/ext*.txt`)
Seven tools fetched as source, built where buildable, run **unmodified** at their claims:

| Tool | Verdict | One-line why |
|---|---|---|
| **udocker 1.3.17, F1 fakechroot** | **works unpatched** | pull→`apk add`→`curl` HTTPS inside alpine; `--allow-root`+`--user=0` (no-passwd root-remap bug). P1/P2 dead: proot `ptrace(TRACEME)` EPERM + misleading launchpad hint; R1 silent rc=4; dpkg trips interposer coverage |
| **ruri 3.9.5** | **works unpatched** | chroot container; every mount/mknod failure is a warning; unshare mode probed-then-refused; apk+curl end-to-end (install resolv.conf yourself; `/dev/null` left absent — shell `>` creates a growing regular file) |
| rurima | pull dead, run works | `tar -xpf` as root → `etc/shadow: Cannot change ownership to uid 0, gid 42: Invalid argument` — §9.1's 5th tenant; non-root path needs proot (dead) |
| dockless | CLI OK, engine dead | guardrails/fail-fast behave exactly as documented; engine is PRoot (F); postgres hook `chown 999`→EINVAL, mknod→EPERM |
| treesandbox | dead | `getpwuid(0)` KeyError, then missing `/etc/hostname` — before any syscall; architecture is unshare+mount with no fallback |
| sandlock 0.8.7 | partial, **one tier unsafe** | Landlock+seccomp+`-m 100M` work; notif tier degrades silently: `--dry-run` **fails open** (prints "no filesystem changes" while the file changes on disk), net ACL fails closed (allowed IP also blocked), `--chroot` exec dead |
| pathshim | honest degrade | `probe`→`passthrough`, reason `EPERM`; never silently maps; reference implementation + preflight for the notif tier |

Kernel model sharpened while testing (F13/F14, `extkernel-newapi.txt` + `extkernel-sources.txt`):
- **F also denies `process_vm_readv`/`writev`** (EPERM for a bogus pid — the kernel would say ESRCH; seccomp cannot fake path/pid-shaped errnos). `pidfd_getfd`/`process_madvise`/`kcmp` execute.
- **New mount API split**: `fsopen`/`fsconfig(CREATE)`/`fsmount`/`open_tree(CLONE)`/`mount_setattr` all succeed — and since 6.18's `fsmount` begins with `may_mount()`, their success proves the capability check passes. `move_mount` returns `ENOENT` for a bogus dest (executes ⇒ **not** filtered) and `EPERM` for real ones — kernel-source proof pins it to `security_move_mount` (the LSM, M), including inside a `clone(CLONE_NEWNS)` child we own. §9.4's "available namespace, unusable mount" now has its exact split: creation/attributes allowed, **attach denied everywhere**.
- Detached mounts are creatable but **not openable** (`openat` → EACCES; fstat shows root-owned world-writable) — an LSM resolving paths cannot resolve a detached mount. v6.18 Landlock hooks (`file_open`, `path_*`, `sb_mount`, `move_mount`, `sb_pivotroot`) suffice to explain every M observation with one ruleset.
- **The notif-supervisor tier is viable**: stacking a `NEW_LISTENER` filter, the notification round-trip, `SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ADDFD` fd injection, and `/proc/<pid>/mem` **read** all work; `/proc/<pid>/mem` write and `process_vm_*` do not. So: intercept + read args + inject fds yes, rewrite child memory no. pathshim and sandlock are the field measurements of exactly that boundary — in opposite honesty directions.

TOOL.md updated: §2.2 extended verdict tables, §5.9's research directions now cite measured tiers (udocker F1 engine tarballs as the interpose shortcut; ruri's warning style; **spec rule: podbox's notif tier must probe {listener, ADDFD, /proc/pid/mem-read} and refuse loudly — never Continue-blind**), field guide +5 rows (proot misdirection, dpkg-under-fakechroot, udocker `--user=0`, dry-run fail-open, getpwuid shim incl. `_r` variants).

Issues: #1–#4 addressed (session 1); #6–#8 filed for the session-2 findings; #2 amended with the move_mount/Landlock attribution.

Fix confirmed on the target after this PR's patch to `probe`'s `check` mode (exit non-zero on failure):

```
mount(MS_SLAVE,/)                  FAIL errno=1 EPERM
mount(MS_SLAVE,/) in clone(NEWNS)  FAIL exit status 1     <- was OK before
```

(`verification/real/probe-census.txt`, plus `umount2` now probed and denied — the §3.2 filter list is target-verified item by item.)

**lilipod v2 status (consolidated 2026-09-07, replaces earlier text)** — patch at `patches/lilipod-restricted-v2.diff` (5 files, +532/−34), evidence in `verification/real/`.

**§5.5 exec: resolved.** v1 built the enter child with `cmd.Env = config.Env`, stripping `LILIPOD_HOME`; the child resolved a *relative* store path, `MkdirAll`-fabricated an empty rootfs, chrooted into it, and `LookPath` failed. v2 inherits the parent env. `exec` works end-to-end, as do `pull/run/create/start/ps/stop/rm/logs`, copy-in volumes, and — via probed `CLONE_NEWUTS` — per-container hostnames.

**Fixes the ten-distro sweep itself surfaced:**
1. **Empty-netns** (v2.1): per-config `CLONE_NEWNET` clones *succeed* on this runtime → routeless netns → silent `ENETUNREACH`. A live §3.4 case.
2. **resolv.conf** (v2.1→v2.3): empty placeholders (AlmaLinux) and baked build-host resolvers (Rocky's `192.168.122.1`) → adopt docker's always-install-host semantics.
3. **OCI whiteouts** (v2.2): void's image ships `/var/cache/xbps -> /var/cache/xbps`; a later layer whiteouts it; plain tar ignores the marker → xbps `ELOOP` (`poc-whiteout-case.txt` reproduces it from the raw layers). v2.2 applies `.wh.*` markers after each layer. Paper §10.4's requirement, now with a live failure case.

**Validation:** ten end-to-end PoCs (alpine, debian, almalinux, arch, void-musl, ubuntu, leap, rocky, rocky-minimal, fedora) — every one builds and runs real workloads through its native package manager; per-manager fixup matrix in `poc-note.md` and paper §8.3. TOOL.md §2.5/§5.3 carry the vs-vanilla-chroot comparison and the full docker/podman parity matrix (`podbox`).

Additional target data supporting the M (path-scoped write policy) attribution, from the extended runs: the four PoCs wrote exclusively inside the allowlist paths (`/tmp` payload tmpdirs, `/workspace` stores) and needed no exceptions — consistent with M being a fixed allowlist, not something derived from mount attributes or mappings. No changes needed to §3.3/§3.7 beyond what the PR carries.
No new information beyond the PR's §8.4 correction; the onelf bundle was not re-packed during the PoC phase, so the unauditable-manifest point stands as written.

**M's mechanism attribution tightened (2026-09-07, second session; #6 carries the full detail).** Three new observations, all M-shaped, from the extended-corpus session:

1. **`security_move_mount` is denied.** `move_mount` executes on the target (ENOENT for a bogus destination — seccomp can't fake that) and returns EPERM for real targets, in the initial mount ns and inside a `clone(CLONE_NEWNS)` child we own. Kernel-source proof pins it to the LSM hook, not the filter and not capabilities: `fsmount()` — which 6.18 guards with the same `may_mount()` check — succeeds here, and `do_move_mount()` has no EPERM site. So M denies *attach*, and §9.4's "available namespace, unusable mount" now has its exact split: fsopen/fsmount/open_tree/mount_setattr all succeed; only attaching is denied.

2. **Detached mounts are unopenable.** `openat` on a detached tmpfs/procfs fd → EACCES (fstat: root-owned, sticky, world-writable — DAC would allow). A path-resolving LSM cannot resolve a detached mount, so every handled access is denied — the same shape as the write-allowlist observations this issue rests on.

3. **`/proc/<pid>/mem` opens read-only but not read-write** (EACCES for O_RDWR) — the write-allowlist applied at file-open granularity, consistent with M being a path-intent LSM rather than anything syscall-shaped.

Landlock v6.18's hook set (`file_open`, `path_*`, `sb_mount`, `move_mount`, `sb_pivotroot`, `sb_umount`, `sb_remount`) is now sufficient to explain *every* M observation with one ruleset — the "Landlock-style" hedge in this issue's original text can be considered upgraded to "consistent with a single Landlock ruleset, pending nothing". Evidence: `verification/real/extkernel-newapi.txt` §2–§3, `extkernel-sources.txt` in branch `target-verification-and-lilipod-v2`.

Related (session 2): the same probe-discipline concern extends past `probe` to third-party tools — a bogus-argument probe (nonexistent path, bad fd, nonexistent pid) distinguishes "seccomp-filtered, pre-execution EPERM" from "executed, denied inside the kernel". That technique settled the move_mount attribution (executes → LSM, not filter) and added process_vm_readv/writev to F's verified deny list (EPERM for a nonexistent pid where the kernel would answer ESRCH). Captured in `verification/real/extkernel-newapi.txt` §1; paper §3.7a item 1. No change to this issue's fix itself.

**Merged into `main` and closed.** All six commits are on `main` (`a8545ee` is an ancestor of `2116846`), so the authorship is preserved and nothing here was rewritten. Closing rather than using the merge button because `main` moved on top of it.

Then it was verified rather than taken. Below is what held, what did not, and what the checking added.

## What held, independently checked

Every kernel-source attribution in `extkernel-sources.txt` verifies against the `v6.18` tag:

| claim | verdict |
|---|---|
| `may_mount()` is `ns_capable(current->nsproxy->mnt_ns->user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)` | ✅ `fs/namespace.c:1992` |
| `fsmount()` and `move_mount()` both open with `may_mount()` | ✅ `:4285`, `:4427` |
| `vfs_move_mount()` calls `security_move_mount()` before `do_move_mount()` | ✅ `:4396` |
| `do_move_mount()` has zero `EPERM` sites | ✅ — and so does `attach_recursive_mnt()`, which the PR did not check but which the attribution also needs |
| Landlock v6.18 hooks `sb_mount`, `move_mount`, `sb_pivotroot`, `sb_umount`, `sb_remount`, `path_*`, `file_open` | ✅ `security/landlock/fs.c:1832-1856` — and `hook_sb_mount`/`hook_move_mount` return `-EPERM` **unconditionally** when a domain handles any FS access, which is exactly the target's signature |
| the target reports Landlock ABI 7 | ✅ `landlock_abi_version = 7` in v6.18 — independent corroboration of the kernel-version claim |

udocker's two mechanisms also read as reported at `638bc42`: `_untar_layers` passes `--no-same-owner --no-same-permissions --exclude=.wh.*` and `_apply_whiteouts` handles `.wh.` and `.wh..wh..opq` itself; `HostInfo().username()` returns `""` on `KeyError` and `engine/base.py` turns that into `invalid syntax for user`.

## What was corrected

1. **The patch is `+532/−34`, not `+343/−34`.** TOOL.md §2.1 and §3 both carried the smaller number; the paper carried the right one. Measured from the diff.
2. **The §8.4 symlink correction replaced one misreading with another.** `references/paper-ox.md:487` says the rootfs "contains 26 **such** symlinks … and 1,558 legitimate relative ones", where *such* means *targets escape the package root* — it does not say absolute, and the one example it gives (`/etc/mtab → ../proc/self/mounts`) is **relative**, and by onelf's own `symlink_target_within_root` would be *accepted*. The "0 absolute, 26 escaping" sanitizer log the issue quotes is not in the corpus. So either the count, the category, or the example is wrong upstream, and no manifest exists to say which. The paper now says that, which strengthens rather than weakens the unauditability point.
3. **`verification/real/cprobe.txt` establishes nothing** and §3.1 cited it for the bare census. It contains `/tmp/cprobe: Permission denied`. Root cause found: the Go probe's chown target and the compiled C probe were **the same path**, so running the census truncated the C probe to an empty mode-0644 file. Fixed (`/tmp/chown-probe-target`).
4. **The v2 lifecycle capture contains a failed run** before the passing one — `ps` printed only its header and `exec` printed nothing, because the detached `start` had not come up within the script's 3-second sleep. `exec` works; a supervisor that decides "running" by sleeping does not. The paper now says so, and `TOOL.md` M4's acceptance test is 20 consecutive passes because of it.
5. **Podman**: the paper claimed "init OK with vfs **[V]**" while `podman-vfs-target.txt` shows 5.8.2 dying at init with a bare `ENOENT` on the target. Both are now carried, with the narrower claim that survives both: the storage driver, not the directory layout, is what stops initialization.
6. **`write into uid-1000-owned dir` in `probe-census.txt` reads `ENOENT`**, which is a missing fixture, not a denial. The probe now reports `SKIP` and exits 2.

## What the checking added

**F16 — the target holds a mount namespace *owned by* its user namespace.** Modelling the target's `0 -> 1000` map made `fsopen`/`fsmount` fail `EPERM` where the target succeeds. `may_mount()` asks for `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` in `mnt_ns->user_ns`, so a user namespace alone is not enough. No prior account named this, and it matters: it is *why* `may_mount()` provably passes on the target, which is what the whole §3.7a attribution rests on.

**Mechanism M is now modellable.** `confine` grew `CONFINE_LANDLOCK`, plus `CONFINE_MAP_HOSTID`, `CONFINE_MOUNTNS` and `CONFINE_DENY_PROCESS_VM`.

**`experiments/` — a containerized reconstruction, with assertions.** Rebuilds the target's identity, mount topology and filter on an ordinary host and checks every attribution row against a written-down expectation. **34 match, 0 fail, 3 skip.** The three that skip are the M rows: this kernel is a Firecracker guest with `CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK` unset, so the script exits 2 rather than passing a run that never tested them. It reproduces the target's identity block byte for byte, `0 1000 1` map included.

It also settles §3.3 cleanly: under N alone, `/usr` `/etc` `/home` `/dev` are denied for exactly the unmapped-owner reason the paper originally gave — and `/` is **writable**, which is precisely the anomaly M exists to explain. Both halves of the argument, one run.

**The bogus-argument technique is now in the instrument** (`probe attribute`, `run.sh attribute`) instead of ad-hoc target-side C.

**Two measurements the corpus did not have:**
- *Language* (`experiments/40-`): Go starts 5 threads before `main()` and cannot `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)` even unconfined; a Go interposer injects 6 threads and 2.0 MB into every process it hooks. Rust: 0 and 312 KB. `TOOL.md` now specifies **Rust**, which drops the lilipod patch as a seed — so every lesson it carried is written out explicitly.
- *The interpose tier* (`experiments/50-`): [pathmap](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/pathmap) `98b3d2a` run unmodified inside the reconstruction. Its preload gives a **bind view with `mount(2)` denied**, and leaves `chown 0:42` at `EINVAL` — identical to the bare call. Its `ptrace` half is dead. Path virtualization and ownership virtualization are separate jobs, and only the second clears the wall that stops five tools. That distinction was collapsed into one bullet before.

## Evidence convention

**[V]** and **[T]** were one tag, which hid a real distinction: a target capture is one observation of a machine nobody else can reach; a **[V]** claim is a command a reader can run. Everything in `verification/real/` and all of §11a is now **[T]**.

Thanks — the target session is what made all of this checkable.

body:
**Fixed on `main`, verified, and two more of the same class found.**

Your fix is in (`verification/probe/main.go`: `check` exits non-zero on failure). It is now verified rather than asserted — in the containerized reconstruction, where the mount *is* denied:

```
mount(MS_SLAVE,/) in clone(NEWNS)      FAIL exit status 1
```

`experiments/results/census.txt`, and the refreshed model run in `verification/results/census.txt` shows the same row flipping from `OK`. `experiments/30-attribution-census.sh` asserts it, so a regression fails the run.

One correction to the record: **`verification/real/probe-census.txt` still shows the pre-fix `OK`** — that capture was taken before the fix and has not been re-taken on the target. The comment above says it was confirmed there. `verification/README.md` now says which captures predate which fix.

## Two more probes were lying, both the same class

Your issue is really about a general rule, so both got fixed with it:

**2. The chown probes and the C probe shared `/tmp/cprobe`.** `chownProbe` did `os.Remove` + `os.Create` on that path — which is also where `run.sh` compiles `cprobe`. So running the census **truncated the C probe to an empty mode-0644 file**, and the next invocation reported `Permission denied`.

That is the entire content of `verification/real/cprobe.txt`:

```
/bin/bash: line 7: /tmp/cprobe: Permission denied
```

The paper cited that file in §3.1 as establishing the bare census. It establishes nothing. The chown target is now `/tmp/chown-probe-target`, and §3.1 says what happened.

**3. `write into uid-1000-owned dir` reported a missing fixture as a denial.** The fixture has to be built by something that can `chown`, which the confined process is not — so on the target it was never created and the row read `FAIL errno=2 ENOENT`, indistinguishable from a real denial. It now returns `SKIP` with the reason, and `check` exits **2** for a missing precondition versus **1** for a denial. `run.sh` also builds the fixture before *any* section rather than before the userns one, which is why the unconfined census used to depend on leftovers from a previous run.

## The rule, written down

`paper_final.md` §10.2 gained a ninth probe rule from this, and §4.1 states it as a property of the instrument:

> A verdict must be the operation's, never a child's exit code unless the child sets it from the operation; and "could not run" must never read as "denied".

Your follow-up point about extending the discipline to third-party tools is also in: the bogus-argument technique is now `probe attribute` and a `run.sh attribute` section, instead of ad-hoc C on a machine nobody else can reach. It is what §3.7a's attributions rest on, and it is reproducible now.

Closing — fixed, verified, and generalized.

body:
**Accepted, and M is now a modelled mechanism rather than a target-only observation.**

Your argument holds: `/` and `/tmp` are both tmpfs created `uid=1000,gid=1000`, both `rw`, in a namespace where 1000 *is* the mapped id — and only `/tmp` accepts a write. Mapping cannot discriminate, and a seccomp filter cannot implement a path allowlist. A third mechanism is required.

## What changed on `main`

**`confine` grew `CONFINE_LANDLOCK`.** A Landlock ruleset that *handles* the filesystem write rights and *grants* them only beneath the allowlisted paths reproduces every M observation at once, and the kernel source says why:

- `hook_sb_mount` and `hook_move_mount` in `security/landlock/fs.c` (v6.18) `return -EPERM` **unconditionally** whenever a domain handles any FS access — so a *write-only* ruleset also denies the whole mount topology, which is exactly the target's signature;
- `hook_file_open` denies an open-for-write outside the allowlist, which is the `/proc/<pid>/mem` O_RDWR row;
- reads stay unrestricted because no read right is handled, which is why the target reads everywhere.

`paper_final.md` §3.2 now carries M as a first-class mechanism with a switch, not as a correction bolted onto §3.3.

**And it is testable now, with an honest gap.** `experiments/` reconstructs the runtime and asserts every attribution row: **34 match, 0 fail, 3 skip.** The three that skip are yours — this kernel is a Firecracker guest with `CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK` unset, so `landlock_create_ruleset` returns `ENOSYS` and the script **exits 2** rather than passing a run that never tested them. On any distro kernel the gap closes. Until someone runs it there, M stays **[T]** + **[S]**, never **[V]** — and `paper_final.md` §12 now opens by saying so, first, before the conclusions.

## The reconstruction sharpened the argument

Running N alone, with the target's own `0 -> 1000` map:

```
/usr denied   /etc denied   /home denied   /dev denied     <- N: owner unmapped
/ WRITABLE    /tmp WRITABLE   /workspace WRITABLE           <- owner mapped
```

Every directory the paper originally attributed to N is denied for exactly the reason it gave — **and `/` is writable**, which is precisely the anomaly M exists to explain. So the original N-explanation and your correction are not rivals: N accounts for the unwritable system directories, and M accounts for the one row N predicts wrong. That is the cleanest statement of what M adds, and it is now in §3.3 with the run behind it.

The §3.3 table gained a row for each case rather than one row with a slash in it.

Your comment about the PoCs writing only inside the allowlist and needing no exceptions is consistent with a fixed allowlist and is recorded. One consequence went into `TOOL.md` §0 as a warning to the implementer: **do not hard-code `{/tmp, /dev/shm, /workspace, /state}` — probe it**, because that set is a single observation of one machine.

Your follow-up (`security_move_mount`, detached mounts, `/proc/pid/mem`) is answered in #6.

Closing — accepted, modelled, and the remaining gap is stated rather than papered over.

body:
**The misquote is real and is corrected on `main` — but not to the figure this issue proposes, and the difference matters.**

You are right that §8.4's "1,558 relative and 26 absolute" was wrong. I could not confirm the replacement.

## What the corpus actually says

`references/paper-ox.md:487` — the original account, unmodified in this repo:

> onelf rejects bundle symlinks whose targets escape the package root … The Arch rootfs contains **26 such symlinks** (all pointing at paths that only exist via mounts, e.g. `/etc/mtab → ../proc/self/mounts`) and **1,558 legitimate relative ones**.

"Such" refers to *targets that escape the package root*. It does not say absolute. And the sanitizer log you quote —

```
absolute->relative: 0, dropped(escaping/missing): 26, ok-relative: 1558
```

— does not appear anywhere in `references/`. I searched all three manuscripts; the only matches are the three prose sentences. So the log is either from the unpublished experiment record or reconstructed from memory. Either way it is **[R]**, and swapping one unverifiable figure for another would have replaced a misreading with a misreading that merely happens to agree with the corrected story.

## And the example contradicts both readings

`/etc/mtab → ../proc/self/mounts` is **relative**, and from `rootfs/etc/` it resolves to `rootfs/proc/self/mounts` — *inside* the bundle. By onelf's own rule (`crates/onelf-format/src/manifest.rs:19`, `symlink_target_within_root`) it does **not** escape and would be **accepted**, dangling or not. `references/paper-astra-corrections.md:533` makes exactly this objection and it stands.

So the original is internally inconsistent: either the count is wrong, or the category is wrong, or the example is not a member of the set it illustrates. No manifest was published to say which.

## What §8.4 says now

The paper states the misreading, quotes what the source actually says, notes that the example is relative and would be accepted, and concludes:

> Either the count, the category, or the example is wrong in the original, and no manifest was published to say which. The substantive point stands and is strengthened: **a transformation nobody can audit is the thing that needed recording.**

F12 in the findings table gained the concrete case — `etc/mtab -> ../proc/self/mounts` is exactly the link the original says was rejected and onelf's rule accepts.

Your closing sentence was right and is why the correction went in at all: the substantive §8.4 point is not weakened by any of this, it is the point. Closing.

body:
**Both findings accepted and on `main`. One thing the evidence shows that the summary did not, and one consequence you will not like.**

## The exec root cause is right, and it is now the paper's

The env-stripped child recomputing the store from an empty environment, resolving a **relative** path, `MkdirAll`-ing a fresh empty rootfs and chrooting into *that* — that is a much better answer than "the lookup is resolving against the wrong root", which is where the review had got to. §5.5 now carries it, and `TOOL.md` §6.5 carries it as an implementation rule:

> Resolve the program in the process that has already changed root, never in the parent and never at command-construction time. And do not strip the environment the child needs to find the store.

`clone(CLONE_NEWUTS)` + `sethostname` is F16-adjacent and equally welcome: it is the one namespace-shaped capability this runtime keeps in usable form, and `--hostname` is **Native** in `TOOL.md`'s parity table because of it. The self-catch about v2 leaking the hostname through the un-flagged exec spawn is exactly the kind of thing worth recording.

## What `lilipod-v2-lifecycle.txt` shows that the summary does not

The file holds **two** runs of the same script. In the first:

```
--- ps:
CONTAINER ID  IMAGE  COMMAND  CREATED  STATUS  LABELS  NAMES
--- exec (was broken in v1):
                                          <- nothing
```

`ps` printed only its header and `exec` printed nothing, because the detached `start` had not come up within the script's `sleep 3`. The second run, identical but for the container name, printed `EXEC-WORKS` and `finalhost`.

`exec` works — I am not disputing that. But **the lifecycle is racy**, and a summary that quotes only the passing run hides the failure that `paper_final.md` §10.6 exists to prevent: deciding a container is running by sleeping and then looking. §5.4 now says this, and it turned into two concrete requirements:

- `TOOL.md` §6.6: *never decide "running" by sleeping and looking* — wait on a pidfd or on a readiness fd the child writes.
- `TOOL.md` M4's acceptance test: **the lifecycle loop 20 times, 20 passes.** One pass proves nothing about a race.

Keeping both runs in the capture was the right call and is why this was findable.

## The consequence: the patch is not the seed

`TOOL.md` now specifies **Rust** for `podbox`, not Go, and the reason is measured (`experiments/40-language-selection.sh`):

| | threads at `main()` | `unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER)` unconfined | threads an interposer injects into its host | interposer size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rust | 1 | **OK** | 0 | 312 K |
| Go | 5 | **EINVAL** | 6 | 2.0 M |

A runtime whose first job is to *probe* namespace availability cannot be written in a language that structurally fails the probe — that is `paper_final.md` F11 turned into a language requirement. And the interpose tier is not optional, so dragging the Go runtime into every `dpkg`, `tar` and `configure` is not acceptable.

So `patches/lilipod-restricted-v2.diff` stays in the repo and will not be applied. To make sure nothing is lost with the code, every lesson it learned is now written out explicitly in `TOOL.md`: the fabricated-root exec bug (§6.5), the racy lifecycle (§6.6), the regular-file `/dev/null` and always-install-host-resolv.conf semantics and the per-layer whiteout requirement (§6.4, §6.3), the empty-netns trap (§8), and the `NoSetGroups` fix (§2.2). Its `getsubids`/`newuidmap`/`newgidmap` dependency check before *any* subcommand is recorded too — that one stops the tool ahead of every syscall wall and is easy to mistake for something deeper.

One correction while measuring: the patch is **`+532/−34`** across 5 files. `TOOL.md` said `+343/−34` and "~340 lines"; your comment and the paper had it right.

Closing — resolved, published, and the parts that generalize are now in the spec.

## The kernel evidence

| your claim | verdict |
|---|---|
| `may_mount()` is `ns_capable(current->nsproxy->mnt_ns->user_ns, CAP_SYS_ADMIN)` | ✅ `fs/namespace.c:1992` |
| `move_mount()`'s only pre-LSM `EPERM` is `may_mount()` | ✅ `:4427`, first statement in the body |
| `fsmount()` starts with the identical check | ✅ `:4285` |
| `vfs_move_mount()` calls `security_move_mount()` before dispatching | ✅ `:4396` |
| `do_move_mount()` has zero `EPERM` sites | ✅ — returns only `EINVAL`, `ELOOP`, or `attach_recursive_mnt()`'s error |
| Landlock v6.18 hooks `sb_mount`, `move_mount`, `sb_pivotroot`, `sb_umount`, `sb_remount`, `path_*`, `file_open` | ✅ `security/landlock/fs.c:1832-1856` |

**One gap in the chain that the issue did not close, now closed:** `do_move_mount()` ends in `attach_recursive_mnt()`, so "zero `EPERM` sites in `do_move_mount()`" is not sufficient on its own — `attach_recursive_mnt()` could have supplied one. It does not; it has no `EPERM` site either. With that, the `security_move_mount()` attribution is airtight rather than merely strongly indicated.

**And the Landlock hypothesis got stronger than "sufficient to explain".** `hook_sb_mount` and `hook_move_mount` do not consult the ruleset's contents at all:

```c
static int hook_move_mount(const struct path *const from_path,
			   const struct path *const to_path)
{
	...
	if (!landlock_get_applicable_subject(current_cred(), any_fs, &handle_layer))
		return 0;
	log_fs_change_topology_path(subject, handle_layer, to_path);
	return -EPERM;
}
```

Any Landlock domain handling **any** filesystem access denies the entire mount topology unconditionally. So a ruleset built only to enforce your write allowlist would produce the `move_mount` denial as a *side effect*, with no separate rule — which is a considerably tighter fit than "one ruleset could explain both".

Corroboration worth noting: the target reports Landlock **ABI 7**, and `landlock_abi_version = 7` in v6.18 exactly. That is independent support for the kernel-version claim as well as for M.

## What is on `main`

`confine` gained `CONFINE_DENY_PROCESS_VM` (F's two extra syscalls) and `CONFINE_LANDLOCK` (M). §3.2's F-list carries `process_vm_readv`/`writev` in the model now, not as a footnote saying the model was not updated.

**The bogus-argument technique is now the instrument**, not ad-hoc C: `probe attribute` and a `run.sh attribute` section. Reproduced on a machine anyone can run:

```
mount(2) bogus target              FAIL errno=1 EPERM     <- filtered
process_vm_readv(bogus pid)        FAIL errno=1 EPERM     <- filtered
pidfd_getfd(-1,-1) [control]       FAIL errno=9 EBADF     <- executed
move_mount(-> bogus dest)          FAIL errno=2 ENOENT    <- executed
```

**Accepted. The notif tier is now a rung on the ladder rather than a footnote, and sandlock is kept as an anti-pattern exhibit.**

## What went into the spec

`paper_final.md` §10.1's mode table gained a `supervise` rung, sitting between `namespace` and `chroot` because it can *deny*, which `chroot` cannot, while providing no namespace. The reason it is a mode and not an implementation detail is your finding:

> `supervise` is the only tier in this table whose failure mode is silent by default. Its argument-reading channel can disappear while its listener keeps working, and a supervisor whose per-syscall fallback is "continue" then reports success for mediation it never performed. A `supervise` mode must therefore probe all three legs — listener, `ADDFD`, argument read — and refuse the tier when any is missing, never fall back per call.

That is your "tier-level precondition, not a per-call soft-fail", promoted from a note about one tool to a rule about the tier. `TOOL.md` §4.1 carries it, and §6.1 makes the three legs part of the required probe set.

Your viability statement is the paper's now, verbatim in substance: **intercept, read arguments, inject fds — yes; write child memory — no.** With one consequence spelled out, since an implementer will hit it: an exec can only be *remapped* by rewriting the pathname in the child's memory, so on this runtime exec mediation can **deny but never remap**.

## The two tools got opposite verdicts, on purpose

`TOOL.md` §7's provenance table uses the verdict vocabulary from the methodology this repo follows, and these two are the clearest cases in the corpus:

- **pathshim — adopt (protocol).** `probe` → `passthrough`, reason printed, non-zero exit, command run unmapped, never silently mapped. Its exit code is a drop-in preflight for the whole tier, and that is how it is described.
- **sandlock — anti-pattern exhibit, kept on purpose.** A shipped defect is worth more than an absence. `--dry-run` reporting `no filesystem changes` while the file changes on disk is the single best argument in the corpus for the loud-degradation rule, and it is cited as such in three places rather than quietly dropped. Its Landlock and seccomp-bpf tiers working unpatched is recorded alongside — the tool is not being written off, one tier of it is.

The direction of each failure is recorded too, because they differ and the difference is the point: COW/dry-run **fails open**, the network ACL **fails closed**. A weaker mode is survivable; a *false report* is not.

## What is verified here versus what stays target-only

Reproduced in the containerized reconstruction (`experiments/`), so anyone can run them:

```
seccomp(NEW_LISTENER)              OK
open /proc/self/mem O_RDONLY       OK
process_vm_readv(bogus pid)        FAIL errno=1 EPERM     <- filtered, not ESRCH
pidfd_getfd(-1,-1) [control]       FAIL errno=9 EBADF     <- executed
```

Still **[T]**: the `NOTIF_ADDFD` round-trip and the `/proc/<pid>/mem` O_RDWR `EACCES`. The second needs Landlock, which this kernel lacks, so `experiments/30-` skips it and **exits 2** rather than passing untested. `paper_final.md` §12 now opens with that gap instead of burying it.

## One measurement your issue prompted

`experiments/50-interpose-tier.sh` runs [pathmap](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/pathmap) `98b3d2a` unmodified inside the reconstruction, because it ships **both** halves of the interpose/supervise problem in one repo — an `LD_PRELOAD` library and a `ptrace` tracer reading the same arguments with `process_vm_readv`:

| | result |
|---|---|
| preload, `PATH_MAPPING=/mapped:/tmp/iv/real`, `cat /mapped/marker` | **works** — a bind view with `mount(2)` denied |
| `chown 0:42` under the same preload | **still `EINVAL`** |
| the `ptrace` tracer | **dead** — `PTRACE_TRACEME: Operation not permitted` |

The middle row is the one worth having: **path virtualization and ownership virtualization are separate jobs**, and only the second clears the wall that stops five tools. That distinction was collapsed in the earlier spec and is now §6.7's central table.

Closing — accepted, promoted into the mode ladder, and the boundary you measured is now measured here too where the kernel allows.

**Accepted, retagged, and two of the mechanisms checked against upstream source.**

Seven tools at their claims is the most useful single contribution in the second session, and §11a carries all of it. Three things changed in how it is recorded.

## Retagged [V] → [T]

Every row of §11a is one session on one machine that no reader can reach. That was tagged **[V]**, the same tag as "run `./verification/run.sh` and see for yourself" — which hid a real difference. The paper now distinguishes:

| tag | means |
|---|---|
| **[V]** | reproduced here, by the model harness or the reconstruction |
| **[T]** | observed on the target and captured, not reproducible here |

§11a is **[T]** throughout, and the section says so in its own opening rather than leaving it to the reader to notice.

## udocker's two mechanisms verified at `638bc42`

The verdicts most load-bearing for the design are the ones with source behind them, so I read them:

- **Ownership-neutral by design** — `container/structure.py::_untar_layers` shells out to `tar -C ROOT -x --one-file-system --no-same-owner --overwrite --no-same-permissions --exclude=dev/* --exclude=.wh.*`, and `_apply_whiteouts` handles `.wh.` and `.wh..wh..opq` itself before each layer. ✅ exactly as reported. This is *why* it clears the §9.1 wall unpatched, and it makes udocker the reference for `TOOL.md` §6.3.
- **The no-`/etc/passwd` remap** — `helper/hostinfo.py::username()` returns `""` on `KeyError`, and `engine/base.py:424` does `if not user: user = HostInfo().username()` before `_user_from_str`, which then fails with `Error: invalid syntax for user`. Line 430 does the `root` → `HostInfo().username()` remap. ✅ upstream bug, worked around by `--user=0`, exactly as you diagnosed.

Those two are marked **[S]** alongside the **[T]**; the rest of the table stays **[T]** with `TOOL.md` §7 telling the implementer to re-verify before building on any of it.

## The corpus became a provenance table with verdicts

`TOOL.md` §7 records every project with its commit, the **depth actually reached**, and one verdict, following the methodology this repo uses:

| | verdict | why |
|---|---|---|
| udocker `638bc42` | **adopt (mechanism), confirms (design)** | extraction flags; `--execmode` is the mode selector the spec asks for, at container granularity. Flagged dormant since 2024-08 |
| ruri `711673a` | **adopt (discipline)** | probe-then-refuse and per-mount warnings are the probe protocol in shipped C. "Copy the style" |
| pathshim `8bcc34e` | **adopt (protocol)** | its `probe` exit code is the notif tier's preflight |
| sandlock `841265d` | **anti-pattern exhibit — keep** | the fail-open dry-run, kept on purpose |
| dockless `ed35b5d` | **adopt (CLI posture), refused (engine)** | fail-fast guardrails are the parity documentation the spec specifies |
| rurima `30a0637` | **refused (pull)** | `tar -xpf` as root; `r` works once a rootfs exists |
| treesandbox `71acbee` | **refused** | `unshare`+`mount` with no fallback |
| PRoot | **refused** | plus the misdirection: it blames an old Ubuntu kernel bug and suggests `PROOT_NO_SECCOMP`, which cannot help |

Your reading (1) — that the ladder has unpatched inhabitants on every rung below `namespace` — is the paper's, and §7.1 states the gap it leaves:

> No project in the corpus does **both** halves of the interposer in one library while also speaking docker's CLI. udocker gets closest, and it is Python, dormant, and inherits fakechroot's coverage ceiling. That gap is podbox.

## One thing measured rather than inherited

`experiments/50-interpose-tier.sh` runs [pathmap](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/pathmap) `98b3d2a` unmodified inside a containerized reconstruction of the runtime. It ships both an `LD_PRELOAD` library and a `ptrace` tracer, so one build measures the surviving route and the dead one:

- preload: **a bind view works with `mount(2)` denied**
- `chown 0:42` under the same preload: **still `EINVAL`**
- the tracer: **dead**, `PTRACE_TRACEME: Operation not permitted`

Which sharpens your reading (3). "Only ownership-neutral extraction or interposition clears it" is now "only *ownership* interposition clears it" — a thorough path interposer does not. §6.7 splits the tier into those two jobs because of this, and the ruri `/dev/null` trap you found (shell `>` silently creating a growing regular file) is in the field guide as a required completion-layer fixup.

Closing — accepted, source-checked where it could be, and honestly tagged where it could not.
